canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats information extraction as directly identifying and extracting structured or otherwise relevant information from unstructured text, and in some cases from semi-structured or multimodal inputs. Many formulations specify the output as entities, relations, events, attributes, facts, values, or field-value pairs, while narrower versions ask for items such as chart titles, axis labels, legend labels, labeled ticks, webpage content, or attributes drawn from tables. Success is usually framed as returning the target items themselves, though some papers instead define it as recalling specific information from extensive interactive histories or as directly extracting attributes from relevant tables rather than retrieving whole tables.

Variants. Papers also use many narrower names for the same broad behavior. Common variants recast it as slot filling, entity extraction, proposition extraction, evidence extraction, and schema extraction, and the surrounding settings range across scientific documents, visually rich documents, charts, tables, webpages, audio, clinical notes, legal text, and dialogue. A recurring difference is the extraction unit: some tasks target short spans or predefined slots, some target structured JSON or table-like outputs, and some treat successful interviewing as obtaining as much information as possible from a source over multiple turns.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers measure it with 11 instruments. The most frequently linked are T-REx, SLURP, ZsRE, FUNSD, and Human evaluation, followed by 6 other instruments. Together these operationalizations span slot-filling datasets, document extraction benchmarks, and human-scored evaluations, with the remaining instruments extending to long-term memory, audio understanding, dialogue, receipt extraction, scientific abstract extraction, and other information extraction tasks.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers do not converge on a single construct that this behavior reflects. The most common linked construct is Reasoning, with one paper claiming a causal relationship from Information extraction to Reasoning and another reporting it is related to Reasoning because reasoning prompts combine visual data, textual prompts, and extracted knowledge. Beyond Reasoning, one paper makes reciprocal causal claims between Information extraction and Hallucination resistance, other papers relate it to Long-context understanding and Long-term memory, and one paper claims a causal relationship from Persuasiveness to Information extraction, while the remaining 3 linked constructs are reported only as related.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats information extraction as directly identifying and extracting structured or otherwise relevant information from unstructured text, and in some cases from semi-structured or multimodal inputs. Many formulations specify the output as entities, relations, events, attributes, facts, values, or field-value pairs, while narrower versions ask for items such as chart titles, axis labels, legend labels, labeled ticks, webpage content, or attributes drawn from tables. Success is usually framed as returning the target items themselves, though some papers instead define it as recalling specific information from extensive interactive histories or as directly extracting attributes from relevant tables rather than retrieving whole tables.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Papers also use many narrower names for the same broad behavior. Common variants recast it as slot filling, entity extraction, proposition extraction, evidence extraction, and schema extraction, and the surrounding settings range across scientific documents, visually rich documents, charts, tables, webpages, audio, clinical notes, legal text, and dialogue. A recurring difference is the extraction unit: some tasks target short spans or predefined slots, some target structured JSON or table-like outputs, and some treat successful interviewing as obtaining as much information as possible from a source over multiple turns.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers measure it with 11 instruments. The most frequently linked are T-REx, SLURP, ZsRE, FUNSD, and Human evaluation, followed by 6 other instruments. Together these operationalizations span slot-filling datasets, document extraction benchmarks, and human-scored evaluations, with the remaining instruments extending to long-term memory, audio understanding, dialogue, receipt extraction, scientific abstract extraction, and other information extraction tasks.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Papers do not converge on a single construct that this behavior reflects. The most common linked construct is Reasoning, with one paper claiming a causal relationship from Information extraction to Reasoning and another reporting it is related to Reasoning because reasoning prompts combine visual data, textual prompts, and extracted knowledge. Beyond Reasoning, one paper makes reciprocal causal claims between Information extraction and Hallucination resistance, other papers relate it to Long-context understanding and Long-term memory, and one paper claims a causal relationship from Persuasiveness to Information extraction, while the remaining 3 linked constructs are reported only as related.
